problem: Prior embodied navigation work transfers only image-level pretrained encoders, while environment-level memory (RNNs, occupancy maps, semantic maps) is either hand-coded or trained end-to-end per task, so it is sample-inefficient and not reusable across tasks.
motivation: Agents need to reason about the larger environment (e.g., inferring that an unseen kitchen likely contains a refrigerator), which needs semantic and geometric priors over sequences of observations. These priors can be learned self-supervised from walkthrough videos collected by other agents, without interactive access to those environments.
key_idea: Pretrain a transformer environment encoder with a self-supervised 'zone prediction' task that masks out geometrically-defined zones of a video trajectory and predicts their features from the seen zones, conditioned on camera pose, using contrastive loss.
insight: Environment-level pretraining on top of image-level MidLevel features gives gains beyond image-level pretraining alone, especially in large environments and on the semantic object coverage task. Pose-conditioned zone prediction matters: SMT (Video), which predicts future frames by time without pose, does not improve over SMT (MidLevel). The method does not need a strong exploration policy or clean sensors, since heuristic-policy videos and noisy depth/pose videos still beat SMT (MidLevel).
method: Zone generation: back-project depth to 3D point clouds, compute pairwise view overlap as the fraction of points with a nearest neighbor within a threshold, then run hierarchical agglomerative clustering on 1-overlap to split each video into zones with little cross-zone overlap.

Zone prediction task: randomly split zones into seen and unseen (4 zones masked per video); given the seen zones' frames (features + pose) and a target pose from an unseen zone, predict that zone's feature, with all poses transformed relative to the target pose.

Transformer encoder-decoder: an MLP M embeds [feature, pose]; the environment encoder applies self-attention to produce environment embeddings E; the zone decoder attends to E using the query pose to output the predicted feature.
NCE loss: the anchor is the predicted feature and the positive is the true zone feature; negatives are other unseen zones in the same video and zones from other videos (temperature 0.1).

Transfer to Scene Memory Transformer: initialize the SMT environment encoder and projection M with EPC weights, replace the end-to-end image encoders with frozen MidLevel features (RGB and depth), and finetune the encoder, policy decoder and policy with DD-PPO.

Pretraining data: ~5,000 500-step RGB-D+odometry walkthroughs from 332 Gibson training scenes (~2M frames) collected by an area-coverage SMT agent or a forward-until-collision heuristic, used for 50 epochs of pretraining.

setting.backbone: Scene Memory Transformer (1-layer encoder/decoder, 8 heads, hidden size 128) with EPC-pretrained environment encoder + frozen MidLevel CNN features, trained with DD-PPO
setting.training_data: Self-supervised EPC pretraining on ~5k walkthrough videos (~2M frames) from 332 Gibson train scenes; then RL fine-tuning on MP3D train scenes for 15M frames per task
setting.observation: 171x128 RGB-D plus odometry pose (x,y,theta) relative to the start

numbers_note: Custom exploration tasks (area coverage, flee, object coverage) rather than standard navigation benchmarks; the numbers are the mean of 3 seeds. Sample efficiency results are only in figures.
results: EPC beats SMT (MidLevel) on all tasks, e.g. MP3D area 172.4 vs 155.6 m2, object categories 9.0 vs 7.6, and instances 36.4 vs 26.8. It is comparable to OccupancyMemory on geometric tasks (which wins on Gibson-L area 67.4 and MP3D flee 14.1) while clearly beating it on object coverage (9.0 vs 7.8 categories). It reaches the best SMT (MidLevel) performance 4-8x faster, and is the most robust under sensor noise (MP3D N-D,P area 159.3 vs 134.2 for SMT (MidLevel) and 85.2 for OccupancyMemory).
limitations: Only tested on exploration-style proxy tasks (area, flee, object coverage), not goal-driven tasks like PointNav/ObjectNav (left as future work).
Pretraining needs RGB-D videos with known poses and camera intrinsics from simulated scans (Gibson); in-the-wild video is not handled. Assumes ground-truth pose and no noise-correction.
OccupancyMemory still wins on some geometric metrics such as Gibson-L area and MP3D flee under noise-free sensing.
